issues.description: New command names break the singular-dash naming convention used by sibling commands.
issues.detail: Existing commands use quickmark-save, quickmark-add, bookmark-add, bookmark-load (singular). The patch registers quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload (plural), and feature tests use :bookmarks-reload. This breaks discoverability and the implicit naming contract. Rename to quickmark-reload / bookmark-reload to match the surrounding code.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic: a parse failure leaves marks empty and emits changed in a half-populated state.
issues.detail: reload() calls self.marks.clear() then re-parses; if _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises, marks ends up empty and changed has already been emitted on an incoherent state. The postcondition should be 'marks matches disk OR previous state is preserved'. Build the new OrderedDict locally and swap on success.

issues.description: New BDD scenarios are unnamed, breaking the feature file's voice.
issues.detail: Both new scenarios are declared as bare 'Scenario:' with no name. Every other scenario in the file has a descriptive title. Anonymous scenarios hurt test-report readability and traceability. Give them names like 'Reloading bookmarks from disk'.

issues.description: Unit test does not cover removal, multi-entry replacement, or the malformed-file failure path.
issues.detail: test_reload only verifies one entry replaced by another. The interesting postconditions — entries removed from disk disappear, additions appear, ordering reflects disk, and parse errors do not corrupt state — are unasserted. Add a multi-entry disjoint-set test and a malformed-reload test to pin the contract.

issues.description: reload() docstring omits pre/postconditions and the discard-unsaved-state behavior.
issues.detail: The one-line docstring does not state the postcondition (marks matches the parsed file, changed emitted once) or the failure mode, and does not warn that reload() silently discards unsaved in-memory changes that the save-manager has not yet flushed. Document the contract so the next maintainer does not have to read the code.

issues.description: Routing __init__ through reload() emits changed during construction, altering the signal's contract.
issues.detail: Previously __init__ populated marks without emitting changed; now it calls reload() which emits changed.emit() at construction time. Subscribers connected at or before construction will see a spurious initial event. Either suppress emission during init or document that changed fires once at construction.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the reload() refactor is the right shape — folding __init__'s parse loop into a reusable method is good taste. Two issues block merge: the new command names (quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload) break the established singular-dash convention used by every sibling command, and reload() is not atomic so a parse error leaves marks empty with changed already emitted. Remaining nits are documentation and test coverage: unnamed BDD scenarios, a thin unit test that doesn't cover removals or malformed input, and a docstring missing pre/postconditions and the discard-unsaved-state warning. Fix naming, parse-then-swap, name the scenarios, and tighten the docstring.
